Stir in the walnuts and pour the batter into the tin.
Bake for 40 minutes; the cake is ready when a toothpick inserted in the middle comes out dry.
Leave in the tin for 10 minutes, then turn out onto a wire rack and cool completely.

Oat and banana cookies
2 tablespoons tahini or hazelnut butter
Preheat the oven to 180°C and line a tray with baking paper.
Mash the bananas with a fork until smooth.
Add the oats, cinnamon, tahini and raisins, mix well and leave for 5 minutes.
With wet hands, roll walnut-sized pieces, place them on the tray and flatten with your palm.
Bake for 15 minutes until golden at the edges.
Leave on the tray for 5 minutes, then cool on a wire rack.
No added sugar; the sweetness comes from the banana.
For young children, chop the raisins finely.
Serve as a snack with milk or yoghurt.
Keeps 4 days in a closed container in the fridge.
Lemon yoghurt cake
Half a cup of sunflower oil
Grated zest and juice of 1 lemon
Preheat the oven to 175°C, grease and flour the tin.
Whisk the eggs and sugar until very frothy.
Add the yoghurt, oil, lemon zest and juice and mix.
Sift in the flour and baking powder and mix with a spatula until lump-free.
Pour the batter into the tin and tap it on the counter a few times to release air bubbles.
Bake for 40 minutes, until a toothpick comes out dry.
Leave in the tin for 10 minutes, turn it out and let it cool.
When grating the lemon zest, avoid the white pith; it makes it bitter.
You can top it with icing sugar or a lemon glaze.
Once cool, slice and serve.
Keeps 3 days in a closed container.
Apple cinnamon muffins
Preheat the oven to 180°C and put paper cases in the muffin tin.
Peel the apples, dice them small and mix with half the cinnamon.
Whisk the eggs and sugar; add the milk and oil.
Sift in the flour, baking powder and the rest of the cinnamon; a few stirs are enough.
Fold most of the apple into the batter and fill the cases two-thirds full.
Divide the remaining apple over the top.
Bake for 20–22 minutes until risen and golden.
Overmixing the batter makes muffins tough.
You can use pear instead of apple.
Serve warm or cold.
Keeps 2 days in a closed container; 1 month in the freezer.
Walnut cocoa cake
1 cup roughly chopped walnuts
Preheat the oven to 175°C; grease and flour the tin.
Add the milk and oil and mix.
Sift in the flour, cocoa, baking powder and vanilla; mix until lump-free.
Fold most of the walnuts into the batter, pour into the tin and scatter the rest on top.
Leave in the tin for 10 minutes, then remove and cool.
Tossing the walnuts lightly in flour stops them sinking.
Leave out the walnuts if there is a nut allergy; the recipe works without them.
Slice once cool.
